text:
BMW is an absolute beast of a game.

The boss fights are easily the highlight. Some of them completely destroyed me at first, but once you learn their patterns and stop panic-dodging everything, the combat becomes incredibly satisfying. Challenging without feeling unfair.
The visuals are phenomenal. The environments, enemy designs, animations and boss fights are genuinely incredible.
I also didn't expect to get this invested in the story and Chinese mythology. The animated stories at the end of each chapter especially caught me off guard — some of them are genuinely beautiful, dark and memorable.
I'm having an absolute blast.
If you like challenging action games, great boss fights and mythology, this is an easy recommendation

Pretty fun. It is somewhat harder than expected. Gameplay wise I prefer the Ashley playstyle. The story is amazing IMO. I'm on my second playthrough, still pretty scary, heh! The graphics are a bit rough, main characters look incredible in cutscenes but, during gameplay, the way the light does it's thing on their faces, look much worse, comparing them side by side. It's night and day.

5 bucks well spent. This is a game that left me wanting more because the gameplay was so fun. Are there only 2 maps? Yeah. Does it take hours to unlock all the gear for each of the 2 characters? Also yeah. Is it a ton of fun if you have a 2nd player in a call with you? Triple yeah. Definitely a worthy pick up for date night.

This game is a delightful combo of Limbo and Little Nightmares. It is simple and short. The art is beautiful.
Things to keep in mind:
This is the Dev's first game - there is less than 3 hours of play time. the video can be glitchy at times. the controls can be clunky occasionally (I played on an XBox controller) 
I found this game on sale and got it for 2.99 - Worth every penny. I will definitely be looking into more content from this Dev. This is an incredible and promising first work.

I love the way it feels to move around and flow from place to place in this game. The grappling mechanic mixed with the picking enemies up mechanic is a great way to mix up the way this game looks like it would play with its mega man influences. the art style and pixel art are so wonderful and the music relaly propels you through the levels. 

I liked exploring all of these levels for the secrets/rescues/upgrades, im happy they had so many, since i liek to take my time in levels like this and find everything anyway. The story was nice, and surprising in some ways, but also besides the story reasons, I really just liked that they committed to everything being a cool looking robot. the power ups you could unlock were all really fun to use, and i look forward to all of my future playthroughs of the game

Very fun game, love the crossplay support! Been playing 4 player coop with two people on Xbox, another on Windoze with the Xbox app and me on Steam flatpak on Linux. The developer is an absolute Chad for enabling Vulkan render support for this game, saves me the overhead of running DXVK. My Windoze buddy says that the DX12 backend aint so great, so I'd recommend adding the '-vulkan' or '-dx11' runtime option. Game runs great on my ancient r9290x

2 hours in and it's shaping up to be one of the best releases of the year. Kyle Thompson continually improves with each game he releases, and doesn't abandon basic principles of metroidvania design for complexity. In a space flooded with soulsvanias and middling waifu shovelware titles, Kyle Thompson is a breath of fresh air in the space. Between him and Team Ladybug, there's nobody else making games in this genre that I'm consistently as hyped for. 

Shame on everyone here for sleeping on his games! You're missing out. His games need way more attention.

It's just like everyone says.  The graphics are picturesque and hit all the right nostalgia feels.  The gameplay and QoL improvements make you feel giddy, like rekindling an old flame.  And the constant stuttering due to horrendous optimization and freezing\crashing due to memory leaks is absolutely disgraceful.  No patches, no acknowledgment, nothing.  Just embarrassing.  I'm powering through it, but I wish I didn't bother. Save your money.

Suit for Hire is a mixed bag. I was pulled in my by the promise of a John Wick style-game from YouTubers. The game does have its Wick moments, and when those happen they are really good, this is due to strong gunplay. However the health system is way too unforgiving, which leads to random difficulty spikes. The enemy AI is also really dumb, to the point where at one point an environmental hazard killed them. However given the unforgiving health system, this is a blessing is disguise, because if they were smart the difficulty would be a nightmare. The game reminds of Hotline Miami, which also pissed me off, this explains a lot, however to be fair the game is way easier due to the checkpoint system, which Hotline Miami lacked. I ended up rage-quitting Suit for Hire and uninstalling the game, so ultimately I lean more negative than positive.

Tainted grail is an absolute masterclass and should be a prime example of how a mythological dark fantasy game should be created, I barely have any clue who these developers are with their background but I am investing in them.  There are some minor flaws here on there, mainly with the performance, but getting behind that, there is seriously such a good game behind it. The combat can be a bit janky at times and takes some getting used to, but the narrative, voice acting, and dynamic and scale of the world carry the experience. This is the type of game I can just look for every nook and cranny and look for some good gear and some little lore scattered across the world, and I love those types of games.
